# Textures

PBR texture sets for the villa scene. Poly Haven assets are **CC0** (public domain, no attribution
required — credited here anyway); the water normal map comes from the **MIT**-licensed three.js
repository and ships with its license notice (`public/assets/textures/water/LICENSE-three.js.txt`).

Regenerate / extend with `npm run assets:textures` (`--force`, `--only=slot,…`, `--check`).
Machine-readable manifest: `src/data/generated/textures.json` (paths are site-relative).

## Conventions

- `color.jpg` — albedo, **sRGB** (`texture.colorSpace = SRGBColorSpace`).
- `normal.jpg` — tangent-space normal, **OpenGL** (+Y) convention (three.js default; linear).
- `arm.jpg` — packed **R = ambient occlusion, G = roughness, B = metalness** (linear). Plug the same
  texture into `aoMap`, `roughnessMap` and `metalnessMap` (three.js reads AO from R, roughness from G,
  metalness from B; since r152 `aoMap` uses `texture.channel`, default UV set 0, so no `uv2` is needed).
  Slots without an ARM map ship `rough.jpg` (grayscale roughness) instead.
- `physicalSize` — real-world width covered by one tile, in metres (from Poly Haven `dimensions`).
- Source resolution 1k JPG. Files over ~700 KB were re-encoded (ffmpeg, chroma layout kept):
  albedo/ARM at ≈ IJG quality 81, normals at ≈ IJG 91 to avoid blocky shading.

## Why these assets

- **ground-meadow** — Sun-bleached straw-coloured dry grass over soil; warm, late-summer Mediterranean, not lush green.
- **ground-garden** — Fine, dark, even garden soil/mulch with tiny petal flecks; reads as tended peristyle beds.
- **path-gravel** — Light warm tan fine gravel; compacted path look without large stones.
- **paving-stone** — Cream travertine-like rectangular slabs with natural pitting; reads as Roman portico/terrace paving.
- **plaster-wall** — Weathered cream/ochre lime plaster with soft patchy wear; tintable for villa walls.
- **roof-tiles** — Irregular orange barrel (coppi-style) terracotta tiles, the closest match to tegula/imbrex roofs.
- **marble** — Seamless cream marble with fine dark veining and no tile joints; works on columns, bench, fountain.
- **rock-cliff** — Pale grey-beige fractured limestone cliff face with warm staining, like the Sorrento/Capri coast.
- **wood-weathered** — Silver-grey sun-weathered untreated planks (coastal/boat wood) for pergola, table and doors.
- **bark** — Grey-brown deeply fissured bark, close to old olive trunks.
- **brick-roman** — Thin, long red bricks with wide mortar beds, proportioned like opus testaceum.
- **water** — Tiling ocean normal map used by three.js examples (Water shader).
